utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I am informed that the parties have met yesterday in the afternoon and that a kind of agreement has been reached on when to cross-examine Mr. Mandic. Of course, before we could move to any scheduling in that respect, I think that it's for the Defence to make an application.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour. In effect, it's -- I understand -- I -- we agreed that I would speak first. In a sense, it's a joint application, I think, reflecting the agreement which we reached, which is, of course, subject -- we're requesting the Trial Chamber's endorsement of the proposals which we have agreed between ourselves. And the -- what is proposed, Your Honour, is this: That the Court, immediately after dealing with this matter now, if the Court approves our agreement, that the hearing should be adjourned until Monday, and on Monday, the witness Mujkic, who has been down for some days, as scheduled for Monday, should be dealt with. That's cross-examination only in relation to that witness, as a Rule 92 bis witness. That on Tuesday, and I understand that it is feasible to schedule the hearings for the rest of that week, leaving aside Wednesday, which is a plenary session for Your Honours and Your Honours' colleagues, that it's possible to schedule the case for afternoons, that we should then begin cross-examination of Mr. Mandic on Tuesday afternoon and continue -- the expectation is that Mr. Mandic would, well, certainly then continue into Thursday and almost certainly into at least a sizeable chunk of Friday. But with the intention and expectation then that it would be possible to conclude Mr. Mandic's cross-examination within those three days. And then the following week, which is the last week before the recess, that the witness Mr. Trbojevic would attend first thing on Monday, would give his evidence in chief in the conventional way and be cross-examined in the -- well, I say the conventional way. See how the cross-examination goes. But according to the conventional procedure. Your Honour, that's the agreement, subject to Your Honours' endorsement that the Prosecution and Defence have reached. Apart from that, it does include -- of course, it's implicit in that that the Prosecution are dropping their contention, if this is agreed and we go ahead on this basis, would then not pursue their contention that we have waived our right to cross-examination. They're not going to turn up on Tuesday and then persist with that point. That's implicit in this. Otherwise, we understand every -- each party has to reserve its position as to any contingencies which may emerge in future. But that's the position as it would be at the moment. I believe that covers it, Your Honour. If Mr. Tieger has anything that I -- well, of course, he will say what he says. If he has anything he believes that I've omitted from what we've agreed, then he can tell us, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I take it that Mr. Stewart has presented your agreement correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean, that's essentially it. The cross-examination will proceed on Tuesday, so in effect, with the adjournment that Mr. Stewart mentioned. So in that sense, we move forward in otherwise the conventional way, as he indicated, and the same with Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Is there any risk that we would have a similar situation as far as the cross-examination of Mr. Trbojevic is concerned? This is not an encouragement to stop whatever disclosure would accommodate the Defence, but the Chamber would like to know whether, if we start Mr. Trbojevic, that we're not confronted again with a situation -- I'm not saying who's to be blamed for it, but just for our assessment of what will be our schedule until the recess, whether there would be any risk that, as it stands now, whether we would have to expect any further requests for the delay of Mr. Trbojevic, his evidence -- the cross-examination of Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I see -- I see no practical risk that we would be in the position of saying to the Trial Chamber that we were not able to start and embark upon cross-examination of Mr. Trbojevic. I can't utterly predict the future, Your Honour, but as I stand here, I see no practical risk of that being the position. Of course, Your Honour, with any witness, it's -- it wouldn't be possible for counsel to say, Well, we can never get to the point where cross-examination might have to go over or be continued at a later date. That's always there inherent in the examination of just about any witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But, Your Honour is specifically, I understand, asking me whether there is any practical, significant risk that we'll be in the same position that we were with Mr. Mandic the other day, and Your Honour, I don't see that as matters stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the Chamber expects, unless matters dramatically change, that once the examination of Mr. Trbojevic would start on the 13th, that he would be cross-examined after that. Then, first of all, I should put on the record that we have been in private session yesterday, and perhaps it would have been more appropriate to, at the very end of the session, to move into open session again. But we started this morning in open session. We discussed yesterday in private session several aspects of the cross-examination of Mr. Mandic and related issues. The Chamber, in anticipation to the -- anticipation of, I think I should say, anticipation of the oral application made this morning, the Chamber has already inquired into whether it would be possible to sit in the afternoon next week. There are courtrooms and Trial Chamber II was so kind to swap with us on the 9th, so that we can also sit on the 9th in the afternoon. Because I have understood that it was part of the agreement and part of the wishes of the Defence. Therefore, the joint application is granted. We'll start on the 6th, also in the afternoon, with the cross-examination of Mr. Mujkic. We'll then, on the 7th, the 9th, and the 10th, during three days, the Defence will have an opportunity to cross-examine Mr. Mandic, and we'll then continue with Mr. Trbojevic on the 13th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, so it is afternoons, apart from the Wednesday, it's afternoons every day that week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's afternoons, apart, I think -- let me just see. On Friday I think, it still has to be arranged, but it has been -- we have made inquiries certainly for the 7th and the 9th, and I take it that it will be possible also to sit in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I hope so, Your Honour, because that was a -- that was an important aspect of the agreement, because -- well, Your Honour can see, if we sit on Friday -- Thursday afternoon and Friday morning, that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll further inquire into that. But I take it that a solution could be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. And Your Honour, we express our gratitude to our colleagues and Your Honours' colleagues in Trial Chamber II for adjustments that may inconvenience them. We do appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said, Mr. Stewart, that Mr. Mujkic was a 92 bis witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I thought that was right, Your Honour. But heads are being shaken, as they often are when I say something. Perhaps I'm -- well, it doesn't -- well, it's obviously correct to get it right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I didn't check it, but I do understand Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond that the cross-examination of Mr. Mujkic is outstanding but that he's not a 92 bis witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. That was just a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mistake -- well, my tongue represented what was in my brain. I was wrong with what was in my brain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then that has been clarified as well. Is there any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the scheduling of travel arrangements for Mr. Mandic has not been finally changed, and of course I also do understand that at this moment, of course, the Prosecution is not in a position to directly contact Mr. Mandic. Should any measure be taken and should we perhaps, because I understand that he is on the premises of the Tribunal, ask Mr. Mandic to come and to explain to him what the situation will be? But Madam Registrar is verifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, while that's happening, may we inquire, because we would understand that given now the relatively short period, that the -- all the normal rules on non-contact and non-discussion while a witness is in the course of his evidence simply apply without qualification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that Mr. Tieger is nodding yes. Does that mean, Mr. Tieger, that the instruction I gave to Mr. Mandic will now be repeated, but now not an open-ended instruction but an instruction for the next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That's what we anticipated, as in the conventional manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then first ask for any information to be provided by the Registry on travel arrangements and on the presence of Mr. Mandic on the premises of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. Two matters, Your Honour. First dealing with this matter. I think the Court may have been apprised as well about the witness's expression of an interest in returning. We leave that to the Court. We think it should be handled in the conventional way. And that is in the interim. I believe you were apprised of that. That should probably be dealt with directly with the witness. And the second matter is the issue of (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was on my mind. So therefore, Mr. Mandic would return and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. We -- I think the witness expressed an interest in that. It seems to me the conventional manner of proceeding with a short delay like this would be for the witness to remain here, but we want just to communicate to the Court, as was done yesterday, his expression of that interest. But again, in view of the circumstances, it seems to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Be appropriate that he remains here and that -- yes. But then, of course, we should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please try to find Mr. Mandic and escort him into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mandic. Good morning, Mr. Tomic. Please be seated. Mr. Mandic, you have become aware yesterday of the opposite positions the parties took in respect of your cross-examination. The parties have further discussed this matter yesterday afternoon, and they have agreed on cross-examination to start on next Tuesday, the 7th of December. The Chamber would like to know whether you could stay until the 7th, then be cross-examined for, as it stands now, for not more than three days. That would be the 7th, the 9th - not on the 8th - and the 10th of December. Could you remain in The Hague in order to be cross-examined next week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber very much appreciates your cooperation and your willingness to stay over the weekend and to be cross-examined next week. Therefore, you're invited to come back to be cross-examined on Tuesday, the 7th of December, in the afternoon, a quarter past 2.00. As it stands now, certainly on the 7th, certainly on the 9th, and presumably also on the 10th, you'll be cross-examined in the afternoon, not in the morning. I would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given and you're still about to give. Yesterday it was more or less an open-ended instruction, because of the special circumstances with a certain uncertainty whether you would be called to be cross-examined. Now this matter has been resolved. It's now not an open-ended instruction any more, but it's at least valid until you reappear in this courtroom on the 7th of December. Then we adjourn until the 7th of December -- yes, Mr. Tieger. You have a --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think the witness can be excused, Your Honour. We have one more matter to attend to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour said adjourned to the 7th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To. No, the 6th. Yes. That's a mistake. Thank you, Mr. Stewart, for reminding me. Mr. Mandic. You're instructed to reappear on the 7th, in the afternoon. We have another procedural issue to deal with at this moment. You're excused for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are speaking, please use the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On behalf of my client and in my own name, I would like to thank this Honourable Trial Chamber, OTP, and the learned colleagues from the Defence for a very correct procedure that has encouraged both me and my client to put trust and place trust in this Tribunal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is an encouraging message for us, and thank you for your kind words. You're excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: (redacted) Your Honour, is what I wanted to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You'd like to do that -- we can do it in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. (redacted) I take it, will have to be changed, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes. I would suggest -- I've not been through this precise procedure, so I'm a bit at the Court's disposal in that regard, but it seems to me an oral modification (redacted) to the witness, which of course is for his benefit so he doesn't have to show up on the date he was subpoenaed and then remain here until the now anticipated date he would be called, so we could readjust that to the date envisioned by our current schedule, which is Monday, the 13th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked Mr. Mandic whether he was in a position to stay until the 7th of December, and it seems that he has not understood that well and that he only understood that he would have to return on the 7th of December. Therefore, I'd like to ask Madam Usher to see whether Mr. Mandic could reappear in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mandic, welcome again. Please be seated. I asked you whether you could stay in The Hague until the 7th and whether you could remain in The Hague until the 7th, but nevertheless, I'm informed that there's some confusion and that you understood this to be whether you could return to The Hague on the 7th. Please tell me if your understanding of what I said was different from what I intended to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said I could not stay in The Hague, that I should actually arrive in The Hague on the 7th, because I came here to stay for three days, and actually I've been here for some 10 or 12 days now. I have to charge my batteries again, be with my family, and then return whenever you say. I have picked up all my belongings from the hotel and was told that I was going to go to the Amsterdam airport for Belgrade after this hearing today. Initially I was informed that I was going to stay in The Hague for three days only, and it's been already 12 now. I have to gather my strength, I have to pull myself together to prepare myself for the examination, and I am psychologically not prepared to stay in The Hague for such a long time. I would appeal to you to allow me to return to be with my family, and then come back here for the continuation of my testimony on the 7th. That's how I understood you. I was yesterday informed that I was going to be escorted to the Amsterdam airport right after this hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest to the parties that we turn into private session and that we further discuss the matter in the presence of the witness, because he's directly affected by the decision we'll have to take. And perhaps we could then also inform the witness about some elements of what we discussed yesterday. Do the parties agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And, Your Honour, when we go into private session, Your Honour will be inviting any submissions from the parties in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But then I will first start to explain some of the elements that we discussed yesterday and then give an opportunity to the parties to make whatever submissions they would like to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, if you speak, please use the microphone. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I kindly ask you to realise the delicacy of the situation. Over the past few days I have witnessed a very serious psychological condition of this man who had come here to testify about the truth and insisting for him to stay here against his will means exerting additional pressure, psychological pressure, and therefore, I'm afraid that he wouldn't be of any use for the purpose of arriving at the truth. I'm afraid that if you decide for him to stay here, that the Defence and the Prosecution will not be on equal footing. He had come psychologically prepared here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please recognise this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, I have no problem that you explain the problems of the witness, but what effect that would have on the equality of arms for the parties is something the parties will discuss. We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On my screen, I see that we're in open session. Mr. Tieger first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Court noted some of the issues raised yesterday before we heard from the witness. It seems to me it has been useful to hear the witness's concerns, which indirectly touch upon some of the issues yesterday. We think great weight should be accorded clearly as in every case to the expressions of the witness and the desires of the witness, and we're confident the Court, as it has demonstrated in the past, feels the same way. So, therefore, we would defer to the Court's decision in this matter, in light of the fact it has now had an opportunity to hear from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although I would do that in private session, in view of the content of our discussions of yesterday. But, Mr. Stewart, any submissions at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour. First of all, the -- the Defence, not surprisingly, Your Honour, would take the position that a witness who has had the opportunity, as Mr. Mandic is requesting, to recharge his batteries, as he puts it, and to spend time with his family should, if at all possible, be given that opportunity. First of all, from the specific and, if you like, narrow, though important point of view that the better refreshed Mr. Mandic is before he returns to be cross-examined, the better all round. The Defence would not wish to have a witness who was, as it is obvious he would be, then resentful that he had not been given that opportunity. Mr. Mandic came freely in the first place anyway. So certainly from the point of view of the conduct of the cross-examination, that situation should, if at all possible, be produced. As a matter of principle, Your Honour, Mr. Mandic, I'm not his counsel, but Mr. Tomic is, but we do support what's said, because as a matter of principle, Mr. Mandic is a -- he is a free person. He came to this Tribunal freely. There is a gap in his evidence. He is required to be in court or needed to be in court on the 7th of December. But otherwise, Your Honour, he should have the basic freedom of any person.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: He should be accorded the basic freedom of any person to come and go as he pleases and as he can. And it would -- it requires the strongest possible reasons which do not exist in this case before a Trial Chamber should in any way presume to restrict that basic freedom. And certainly the matters which have been touched on in private session, which of course I'm not going to then explore in open session, but they do not justify it. That would be an extraordinary presumptive thing to impose upon somebody like Mr. Mandic, who does not want -- does not himself express and does not want those concerns - that's quite clear - to be dealt with by any restriction upon his freedom. That would be an extraordinary step to take. There is no suggestion that's been made in private, or in open session, that there's any significant danger or risk to the evidence that this witness would then give when he returned. So Mr. Mandic is a free man and should be permitted freely to go back home for the weekend and is of course then expected to come back on Tuesday, and there's not the slightest indication that he won't be back on Tuesday. He came freely in the first place, and there's no reason whatever to doubt that he will be here to be cross-examined on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just a small note, Your Honour, to -- that is, that the Prosecution, of course, supports the fundamental principles expressed by Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has heard the parties and the Chamber has heard you, Mr. Mandic, on several aspects of the question whether we should ask you to remain in The Hague or whether we would allow you to return to your family and then come back on the 7th of December. The Chamber allows you to return to your family. And you're instructed, as I instructed you before, not to speak with anyone about your testimony already given or still to be given. This includes that you should refrain from any contact with the media. You explained to us that you want to reload your battery in your family situation. I think if you are in the -- in a circle of your family, it will be even easier for you to reload your battery and not to -- and to refrain from any contact with the media. The Chamber also sees that the matter was quite emotional for you, and the Chamber understands why it is. Then, Mr. Mandic, perhaps we should have taken more care not to bring you from one extreme to another, since this might not have been easy for you. Our apologies if we caused any confusion. But looking at the transcript, I think it was just a matter of misunderstanding of my question, and perhaps I should have verified better whether you understood me well. You're excused. I take it that you'll reappear, as you did before, voluntarily next Tuesday. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: (redacted) This is a technical matter. You don't have to be concerned about that. You're excused. I would like to see you back next --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry for intervening which in a sense I am, because I have one further submission, which in this case I suggest ought to be made while Mr. Mandic and his counsel are still here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's this: That in the light of what has occurred this morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, for scheduling reasons of travelling of the witness, we have two minutes left, before otherwise he misses his plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the light of everything that's been said this morning and particularly what the witness has said specifically in answer to Your Honour's suggestion of concerns of his position when he returns to Serbia, it's quite clear now that the -- that all the discussion which has taken place in private session yesterday and today should now -- the transcript should be open. There is no justification for that material remaining private. It's all quite clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll consider that, whether the transcript will be redacted in the sense that what has been said in private session should be public. We'll consider that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Redacted, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Redacted. Amend -- no, redacted, I mean that where it says private session, that it would then be public again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Open. Yes, Your Honour. That's our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll consider that. Mr. Tomic, thank you for your presence. Mr. Mandic, I hope that you have a weekend in which you really can reload your battery, and we'd like to see you back Tuesday in the afternoon. You're excused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any other issue to be raised?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Without reviewing the transcript again, Your Honour, I just want to indicate that we oppose counsel's motion. We may get together on that and discuss it while the Court is considering it. I don't know if there will be any need for submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you could please exchange your views on that, see whether that brings any new situation. I mean, it's not that urgent that it should be done today.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No. I agree, Your Honour. May I just say, depending how far we get with discussions, if then in effect -- it amounts, in practice, we suggest, to an application to justify continuing withholding that material from the public, so we therefore would like, if it comes to it and we can't reach agreement, we would like the opportunity of meeting and making submissions in relation to whatever is suggested to be the justification of continuing to withhold that material from the public. It's a procedural --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber will then hear further from the parties. We stand adjourned until the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until next Monday, and the parties will be informed about time and courtroom. Because there seems to be some confusion. The parties will be informed today. Yes, we're adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of December, 2004 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.05 a.m.,
